headline: Application Support Engineer | Linux | SQL | AWS
summary: Cloud and DevOps Engineer who troubleshoots from evidence rather than guesswork: decoded a live GitHub OIDC token to fix an AWS trust-policy failure, traced an AWS AuthFailure to clock skew from blocked NTP, and writes incident reports with root cause and corrective actions. Operates an enterprise-style RHEL environment through tickets and runbooks, with Linux, SQL, REST APIs and AWS.

bullets.text: Completed 30 hands-on labs across build tools (Gradle, Maven), Docker, Jenkins, Kubernetes, ArgoCD and Ansible, each documented with its objective, steps and verification.
Completed intensive hands-on training in Linux administration, networking, CI/CD, containerization, and cloud infrastructure, culminating in end-to-end DevOps projects (see Projects).

bullets.label: Automation & Operations
bullets.text: Idempotent Ansible roles (EC2 dynamic inventory) handle SSH hardening, SELinux, firewalld, chrony and fleet patching; Bash scripts rebuild and test the lab, with tickets, runbooks and incident reports documenting changes.

bullets.label: Identity & Team Policy
bullets.text: FreeIPA centralizes users, DNS, Kerberos, HBAC and sudo rules per team; the utility server runs a Squid proxy with per-team internet rules, NFS home directories, centralized logging and backups.
Fixed a GitHub Actions OIDC trust-policy failure by decoding the live JWT, finding the immutable numeric IDs in its sub claim, and building the correct wildcard with Terraform replace().
Resolved a kube-prometheus-stack ArgoCD sync failure caused by the Kubernetes 262144-byte annotation limit by enabling ServerSideApply.

bullets.label: Platform & Security
bullets.text: Five Python/FastAPI banking microservices and an NGINX frontend on EKS, built for financial correctness (fencing tokens, row-lock ordering). Versioned Terraform modules deploy through GitHub Actions (OIDC) and ArgoCD App-of-Apps, secured with default-deny NetworkPolicies, Istio mTLS, Gateway API and External Secrets Operator (IRSA).
Wrote Pytest async integration and concurrency tests for the transfer path.
Streamed logs to CloudWatch Logs and set four CloudWatch metric alarms that notify by email through SNS.
Wrote a failure test that stops a backend, measures traffic continuing on the healthy instances, restores it and proves recovery, plus backup and restore of the database.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Application Support Engineer role at Pyramid Pay in Cairo. I solve infrastructure problems methodically and document them so they stay solved. My background is Linux, SQL, REST APIs and AWS, and I troubleshoot from evidence rather than guesswork.

Linux and log analysis: in my RHEL lab on AWS I ran incident drills for an identity outage and a full log disk, documented in 7 incident reports with root cause and actions. I also traced a Terraform AuthFailure to about 14 minutes of clock skew on a machine where outbound UDP 123 (NTP) was blocked, and fixed a GitHub Actions OIDC failure by decoding the live JWT. SQL and REST APIs: I built five Python/FastAPI microservices on Amazon RDS MySQL for the Nexora banking platform and wrote Pytest async integration tests for the transfer path.

Troubleshooting is the part of the work I already do every day: reading logs, narrowing a cause with evidence, fixing it, and writing the runbook. A support role puts that skill directly in front of users and production systems. I work through tickets and runbooks in my lab, so a ticket-driven support workflow is familiar. I would welcome a conversation about how I can help your support team, and my CV is attached.

email_body:
Hello,
I am applying for the Application Support Engineer role at Pyramid Pay.
My CV and cover letter are attached.
I work with Linux, SQL, REST APIs and AWS, and I document every incident with root cause and actions.
I would be glad to discuss the role.
why_this_role: Tracing an AWS AuthFailure to NTP clock skew and writing 7 incident reports with root cause and actions in my RHEL lab is the same evidence-based troubleshooting an application support role needs.
